title: POC Weekly Sync - App Integration / SDK + Tool & Function Calls / Structured Output
summary: Weekly POC check-in to review pilot results integrating Redwood SDK into HarborPay app flow. Discussed function/tool calling reliability, structured JSON outputs for transaction summarization, latency tradeoffs, and next steps: run 1k-transaction benchmark, share security whitepaper, and schedule on-site performance test with Dedicated capacity pricing options.
topics: structured output schema for transaction summaries
action_items: Maya Patel: Share Dedicated pricing sheet and perf faq by 2026-04-18
Omar Ruiz: Provide sample SDK snippet for retry/backoff and tool-call handling by 2026-04-17
Priya Menon (HarborPay): Send list of compliance questions for SOC2/KMS by 2026-04-20
Samir Shah (HarborPay): Run 200-transaction smoke test with KV cache on 2026-04-16 and share logs
next_steps: Redwood to run 1k-transaction benchmark with HarborPay payloads (redwood/internal) - target week of 2026-04-20
HarborPay to enable SDK telemetry and share sampling data
Schedule follow-up on-site perf test if benchmark meets latency SLOs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42 minutes | Location: Zoom | Recording: yes
Attendees (as on call): Maya (Redwood AE), Omar (Redwood SE), Jin (Redwood SE), Avery (Redwood CSM), Lena (HarborPay PM), Samir (HarborPay BE), Priya (HarborPay Sec/Infra), Ethan (HarborPay Data Sci)

00:00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone thanks for hopping on, quick roll call — can everybody hear me?
00:00:05 - Lena: Yep, loud and clear.
00:00:07 - Samir: Yep.
00:00:10 - Priya: here.
00:00:12 - Maya: Awesome. Alright quick agenda — one: integration status and blockers, two: results from the structured output tests you ran, three: perf tuning (latency/batching/kv cache), four: security/compliance Qs, and five: next steps. Sound good?
00:00:27 - Lena: Sounds good.
00:00:29 - Maya: Cool. Omar do you wanna start with SDK integration notes?
00:00:33 - Omar: Yeah for sure, thanks. So we looked at HarborPay's SDK usage — you wired up the node/python SDKs and you're calling the generate/chat endpoint with the function_calls enabled, right? The flow Samir sent earlier where you call the tool for ledger lookups then the function to build the transaction summary. That's correct?
00:00:50 - Samir: Yep that's the flow. We had to add an adapter because our payments engine expects a strict JSON schema, otherwise some of the ai text was coming back a bit freeform.
00:00:59 - Omar: Right and that's where the structured output setting comes in. We recommended the SDK config with schema validation + deterministic mode for the structured output tests. Jin can add specifics but basically you set the model params, pass the schema, and the SDK will return the parsed object in the response.
00:01:13 - Jin: Yeah, one note — the SDK currently has two patterns: function_call-first where the model returns a function call object, or structured-output where the model is constrained to emit json. For HarborPay we used function_call to trigger the summarize_transaction function, which returns a JSON payload, and then we validate client-side. We also showed the structured-output path which uses 'response_schema' to enforce field types server side.
00:01:33 - Lena: We tried both. The function_call pattern is easier for iterative flows but we saw occasional gibberish fields when the model fell back to the hosted variant with a higher temperature. The structured schema approach was more consistent but slightly slower.
00:01:47 - Omar: That matches what we expect — schema enforcement adds a bit of decode/validation overhead and sometimes triggers a re-sampling step. Latency hit was about 30 to 80ms on average in our small tests.
00:01:58 - Samir: For us the big concern is throughput during peak — we can't have the payment confirmation flow add more than 200ms p95. Right now on your hosted setup we saw p95 around 280ms when batching was off, but with batching enabled we got it down to ~180ms but that increased cost per token slightly.
00:02:14 - Maya: Important point — there's always a tradeoff. For the POC we recommended experimenting with continuous batching and prefix caching. Omar, can you remind them about KV cache for session context?
00:02:24 - Omar: Sure. So Redwood's SDK and runtime can persist the model key value cache for a user session — that reduces repeated prompt tokens for subsequent calls. For HarborPay's flow, since most calls are short and the model uses the last 2-3 turns, enabling KV caching cut median token usage by about 45% in our sim. That also reduced latency because batching didn't need to re-send big context.
00:02:43 - Priya: Quick question on KV cache — where is that stored? Is it in our VPC or on Redwood managed infra?
00:02:50 - Jin: Good question. For hosted POC KV cache lives on Redwood managed edge nodes; for Dedicated or Private we can run KV cache inside your VPC or on-prem depending on the deployment.
00:02:59 - Priya: Okay that's what we thought — we'll need it in-VPC for production because of our data residency rules.
00:03:05 - Maya: Noted. We'll follow up with Dedicated pricing.
00:03:08 - Lena: On structured output content — Ethan ran the transaction summarizer across 500 historical transactions and we compared machine output to gold labels. Accuracy is good for amounts, currency, merchant, and four fields, but we see a lot of variance in the "merchant_category" and "intent_flags" fields. Model is hallucinating categories for ambiguous descriptions.
00:03:28 - Ethan: Yeah I can share the confusion matrix and a few examples. It's mainly short freeform memos in the description field that cause it.
00:03:34 - Omar: Two approaches — one is prompt engineering + stricter schema enums for merchant_category to force a small set; second is a reranker/heuristic that checks the model output against transaction metadata before accepting. We can also add a tool-call to your internal merchant classifier if you prefer.
00:03:48 - Samir: Tool call would be ideal: flow would be (1) model returns function_call with merchant_name, (2) Redwood runtime calls HarborPay merchant-classifier internal service, (3) we return the normalized category and model finalizes the JSON. Is that supported?
00:04:02 - Jin: Yes — that's the tool-calling pattern. The runtime can call external services as tools if you register them in the SDK. We have prebuilt adapters and the SE team can help wire the auth — OAuth or mTLS.
00:04:12 - Priya: Auth — we need mTLS and request logs forwarded to our SIEM. Is that doable for tool calls?
00:04:18 - Omar: Yes, for Dedicated or Private deployments we can do mTLS and push logs into your logging endpoint. For hosted we can route logs via an encrypted pipeline but some customers prefer the Dedicated path for full control.
00:04:28 - Priya: Okay that's helpful.
00:04:31 - Maya: Let's jump into the benchmark results you ran last Friday — Samir, can you summarize what you ran?
00:04:36 - Samir: Sure. It was 200 transactions parallelized across 20 threads using the SDK default retry logic. We toggled KV cache and batching. Results: no batching + no kv: median 160ms, p95 280ms. Batching 8 + kv enabled: median 110ms, p95 170ms. Structured schema enforced: added ~45ms median, p95 bumped to 220ms in the no-batching case.
00:05:02 - Maya: Thanks. Omar, anything to add?
00:05:05 - Omar: Just that the SDK snippet we recommended includes async streaming and early parse of the JSON so you can start accepting fields as they arrive which reduces perceived latency. Also set 'max_tokens' tightly — avoid huge token windows.
00:05:17 - Ethan: One odd thing — some responses had truncated JSON and SDK parse failed, then our code retried and got duplicate transactions in the ledger because retry dedupe wasn't complete. Any suggestions?
00:05:29 - Jin: That's a classic at-least-once problem. We recommend idempotency keys on your side and the SDK's idempotency helper. Also use the SDK's partial-response safe-parser which can detect truncation and request just the missing portion using the model's function calling to re-request only the missing fields.
00:05:45 - Lena: Will that add more calls and cost?
00:05:48 - Omar: Slightly, but it's minimal if you only request the missing slice. It beats writing complex dedupe logic in the payments path.
00:05:54 - Priya: Security, one more: KMS integration. We need to wrap keys in our Google Cloud KMS and have Redwood never see plaintext keys for our private deployment. Is that possible?
00:06:05 - Maya: Yes, Private or Dedicated with bring-your-own-key is supported. We'll work with infra to detail KMS/HSM flow. We'll send the security whitepaper.
00:06:14 - Priya: Great.
00:06:16 - Maya: Ok quick pivot — pricing and Dedicated options. I'll drop the pricing sheet but wanted to highlight that Dedicated pricing includes an option for reserved capacity plus overage. If you need 99ms p95 at scale we'd recommend a "burst" pool + a pinned model lane. We'll include sample numbers in the sheet.
00:06:33 - Lena: Do you have a cost estimate for the continuous batching approach vs low-latency single-shot?
00:06:38 - Maya: Quick rule of thumb: batching reduces tokens per call by ~30-50% depending on context reuse but increases per-call latency if your app requires immediate single-turn responses. We'll include modeled numbers for HarborPay's observed traffic pattern in the sheet.
00:06:52 - Samir: For our MVP, if we hit average 300 TPS bursts could be 1k qps — what's Redwood's recommended architecture?
00:07:00 - Omar: For that scale Dedicated with autoscaling GPU pools is ideal. Smart routing can fall back to a cheaper model for lower-priority background tasks. For mission critical confirmations you'd stay on pinned lanes. We'll outline an architecture doc.
00:07:12 - Maya: Cool. Back to structured output: any open items on the schema?
00:07:16 - Ethan: We updated schema v2 last night to add a merchant_confidence float and intent_flags as an enum set. But the model still sometimes emits freeform text in intent_flags.
00:07:28 - Jin: We can add post-validators in the SDK that coerce or call your internal classifier as a tool. Also consider adding a small verification model — a lightweight reranker — that accepts the candidate JSON and scores it against the gold. That reduces hallucinations.
00:07:42 - Lena: Could Redwood run that reranker as part of the runtime or would that be an extra service?
00:07:46 - Omar: We can host a lightweight reranker on Dedicated pools or call your service as a tool; either works. If you want lowest latency, co-located reranker inside your VPC is best.
00:07:56 - Priya: For acceptance criteria — we need p95 < 200ms and merchant_category accuracy > 95% on the gold set. Is that feasible?
00:08:06 - Maya: Feasible with Dedicated + KV cache + co-located classifier/reranker. For POC we should try to hit p95 < 200ms with batching and see if accuracy improves with the tool pipeline.
00:08:16 - Lena: Ok let's commit to that.
00:08:18 - Maya: Quick logistics — action items recap. Maya will send pricing and architecture docs. Omar will share SDK snippet and sample telemetry setup. Jin will provide a tool-call example with mTLS config. Samir and Priya will run the smoke tests and send logs. Ethan will send the evaluation dataset and results. Anything else?
00:08:36 - Samir: We'll also add idempotency keys to our ledger calls.
00:08:38 - Maya: Good.
00:08:40 - Lena: One more tiny ask — can you share the sample curl/sdk call that demonstrates streaming partial JSON parse? Our mobile team wants that.
00:08:48 - Jin: Yep we'll include an example repo link and a small snippet — I'll upload to the shared deck.
00:08:55 - Maya: Great. Any competition concerns? Priya?
00:08:58 - Priya: Nothing new, we've evaluated Anthropic and Bedrock; primary blocker for Redwood is proving latency and KMS integration.
00:09:07 - Maya: Understood. We'll prioritize the Dedicated trial for you.
00:09:11 - Lena: Ok timeline — can we aim for the 1k transaction benchmark the week of 2026-04-20?
00:09:18 - Maya: Yes we'll run it internally and share results. If good, schedule on-site perf test the following week.
00:09:24 - Samir: Sounds good.
00:09:26 - Maya: Cool any final questions?
00:09:28 - Ethan: Quick question — telemetry retention, how long do logs stick around in hosted POC?
00:09:33 - Omar: By default 7 days for detailed telemetry, 90 days for aggregated metrics. We can extend retention for an enterprise add-on or on Dedicated in your infra.
00:09:44 - Priya: We'll need 90+ days for audit, preferably forwarded to our SIEM.
00:09:48 - Maya: We'll include the logging forwarding plan.
00:09:51 - Lena: Alright thanks everyone. Recap and next steps?
00:09:55 - Maya: Recap: Redwood to share pricing, SDK snippets, tool-call/mTLS example, and run 1k benchmark week of 4/20. HarborPay to run smoke tests, send dataset + questions, and confirm KMS requirements. We'll reconvene next Friday same time unless otherwise noted.
00:10:12 - Lena: Works for me.
00:10:14 - Maya: Thanks all — talk soon.
00:10:17 - meeting end

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript had a few mislabels and occasional dropped punctuation — we kept original speaker labels where possible. Some technical terms spelled out in full in the notes (KV cache, mTLS).
